units.zh: 盧光稠譚全播
units.en: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo
units.literal: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo

units.zh: 盧光稠、譚全播，皆南康人也。
units.en: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo were both men of Nankang.
units.literal: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo were both natives of Nankang.

units.zh: 光稠狀貌雄偉，無佗材能，而全播勇敢有識略，然全播常奇光稠為人。
units.en: Guangchou looked the part of a warlord but had little else to recommend him. Quanbo was brave and shrewd, yet he kept finding something remarkable in Guangchou’s character.
units.literal: Guangchou was imposing in bearing but had no other talent, while Quanbo was brave and possessed foresight—yet Quanbo often marveled at Guangchou as a man.

units.zh: 唐末，群盜起南方，全播謂光稠曰：「天下洶洶，此真吾等之時，無徒守此貧賤為也！」
units.en: As Tang collapsed, rebels swarmed the south. Quanbo told Guangchou: “The empire is boiling over. This is our moment—don’t waste it clinging to poverty and obscurity!”
units.literal: At the end of Tang, bandits rose throughout the south. Quanbo said to Guangchou: “The realm is in uproar—this is truly our hour; do not merely sit guarding this poverty and low station!”

units.zh: 乃相與聚兵為盜。
units.en: They raised men and turned to the hills.
units.literal: They then together gathered troops and became bandits.

units.zh: 眾推全播為主，全播曰：「諸君徒為賊乎？
units.en: The men wanted Quanbo as their leader. Quanbo said: “Do you mean to stay mere bandits?
units.literal: The crowd wished to make Quanbo chief. Quanbo said: “Do you gentlemen wish only to be bandits?

units.zh: 而欲成功乎？
units.en: Or do you mean to win something that lasts?
units.literal: Or do you wish to achieve success?

units.zh: 若欲成功，當得良帥，盧公堂堂，真君等主也。」
units.en: If you want to last, you need a real commander. Master Lu has the bearing of a lord—he is the man for you.”
units.literal: If you wish success, you must have a worthy commander. Master Lu is imposing—he is truly your proper lord.”

units.zh: 眾陽諾之，全播怒，拔劍擊木三，斬之，曰：「不從令者如此木！」
units.en: The men nodded along. Quanbo flew into a rage, drew his sword, and hacked a wooden post three times until it fell. “Disobey,” he said, “and you go the way of this timber!”
units.literal: The crowd pretended to agree. Quanbo in anger drew his sword and struck a post three times, cut it down, and said: “Whoever disobeys the order shall be like this post!”

units.zh: 眾懼，乃立光稠為帥。
units.en: The men quailed, and Guangchou was made commander.
units.literal: The crowd was afraid, and thereupon installed Guangchou as commander.

units.zh: 是時，王潮攻陷嶺南，全播攻潮，取其虔、韶二州，又遣光稠弟光睦攻潮州。
units.en: Wang Chao had seized Lingnan. Quanbo struck back, took Qian and Shao from him, and sent Guangchou’s brother Guangmu against Chaozhou.
units.literal: At that time Wang Chao had overrun Lingnan. Quanbo attacked Chao and took his Qian and Shao prefectures, and also sent Guangchou’s younger brother Guangmu to attack Chaozhou.

units.zh: 光睦好勇而輕進，全播戒其持重，不聽，度其必敗，乃為奇兵伏其歸路。
units.en: Guangmu was brave and reckless. Quanbo told him to keep his weight behind the line; Guangmu ignored him. Quanbo read the defeat coming and hid men on the road home.
units.literal: Guangmu was bold and rash in advance. Quanbo warned him to hold his ground; he would not listen. Quanbo judged he must fail and therefore laid an ambush on his line of retreat.

units.zh: 光睦果敗走，潮人追之，全播以伏兵邀擊，大敗之，遂取潮州。
units.en: Guangmu broke and ran. Chao’s men gave chase. Quanbo sprang the ambush and shattered them, then took Chaozhou.
units.literal: Guangmu was indeed defeated and fled. The men of Chao pursued him. Quanbo struck with his hidden troops, routed them utterly, and thereupon took Chaozhou.

units.zh: 是時，劉巖起南海，擊走光睦，以兵數萬攻虔州。
units.en: Liu Yan was rising on the southern coast. He brushed Guangmu aside and marched tens of thousands of men on Ganzhou.
units.literal: At that time Liu Yan rose in the southern sea, drove off Guangmu, and with tens of thousands of troops attacked Ganzhou.

units.zh: 光稠大懼，謂全播曰：「虔、潮皆公取之，今日非公不能守也。」
units.en: Guangchou was terrified. He told Quanbo: “You won Qian and Chao for us. Only you can hold them now.”
units.literal: Guangchou was greatly afraid and said to Quanbo: “Qian and Chao were both taken by you; today if not for you they cannot be defended.”

units.zh: 全播曰：「吾知劉巖易與爾！」
units.en: Quanbo said: “Liu Yan is nothing I cannot handle!”
units.literal: Quanbo said: “I know Liu Yan is easy to deal with!”

units.zh: 乃選精兵萬人，伏山谷中，陽治戰地於城南，告巖戰期。
units.en: He picked ten thousand elite men and hid them in the hills, staged a battlefield south of the walls, and named a day to fight.
units.literal: He then chose ten thousand picked troops, hid them in mountain valleys, openly prepared a battlefield south of the city, and notified Yan of the day of battle.

units.zh: 以老弱五千出戰，戰酣，偽北，巖急追之，伏兵發，巖遂大敗。
units.en: He marched out five thousand aged and weak soldiers, fought until the heat of battle, then pretended to break north. Yan rushed after him. The ambush rose; Yan’s army collapsed.
units.literal: With five thousand old and weak he went out to battle; when the fight grew hot he feigned defeat to the north. Yan pressed the pursuit in haste; the hidden troops sprang forth and Yan was utterly routed.

units.zh: 光稠第戰功，全播悉推諸將，光稠心益賢之。
units.en: When honors were handed out, Quanbo gave every laurel to his generals. Guangchou admired him all the more for it.
units.literal: When Guangchou ranked battle merit, Quanbo pushed all credit to the generals, and Guangchou’s heart esteemed him all the more.

units.zh: 梁初，江南、嶺表悉為吳與南漢分據，而光稠獨以虔、韶二州請命於京師，願通道路，輸貢賦。
units.en: Early in Liang, Jiangnan and Lingnan were carved up between Wu and Southern Han. Guangchou alone held Qian and Shao, bowed to the court, and asked for roads and tribute.
units.literal: At the beginning of Liang, Jiangnan and Lingnan were all divided between Wu and Southern Han, while Guangchou alone with Qian and Shao two prefectures submitted to the capital, wishing to open roads and deliver tribute.

units.zh: 太祖為置百勝軍，以光稠為防禦使、兼五嶺開通使，又建鎮南軍，以為留後。
units.en: Liang Taizu Zhu Wen raised the Hundred Victories Army, made Guangchou defense commissioner and commissioner to open the Five Ridges, then founded the Pacify-the-South Army and kept him as military governor.
units.literal: The Founder established the Hundred Victories Army, made Guangchou defense commissioner and concurrently commissioner for opening the Five Ridges, and also raised the Pacify-the-South Army and made him its military governor.

units.zh: 開平五年，光稠病，以符印屬全播，全播不受。
units.en: In Kaiping 5 (911) Guangchou fell ill and pressed his seals on Quanbo. Quanbo refused.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiping, Guangchou fell ill and entrusted his seals to Quanbo; Quanbo would not accept them.

units.zh: 光稠卒，全播立其子延昌而事之。
units.en: Guangchou died. Quanbo set up his son Yanchang and served him loyally.
units.literal: Guangchou died; Quanbo installed his son Yanchang and served him.

units.zh: 延昌好遊獵，其將黎求閉門拒延昌，延昌見殺。
units.en: Yanchang lived for the hunt. His general Li Qiu barred the gates against him and had him killed.
units.literal: Yanchang loved hunting and sport. His general Li Qiu shut the gates and barred Yanchang; Yanchang was killed.

units.zh: 求因謀殺全播，全播懼，稱疾不出。
units.en: Qiu plotted Quanbo’s death next. Quanbo took fright, claimed illness, and would not leave his house.
units.literal: Qiu then plotted to kill Quanbo as well. Quanbo was afraid and pleaded illness, not coming out.

units.zh: 求乃自立，請命於梁。
units.en: Qiu seized power for himself and sued for recognition from Liang.
units.literal: Qiu then installed himself and submitted to Liang.

units.zh: 乾化元年，拜求防禦使。
units.en: In Qianhua 1 (911) Liang made Qiu defense commissioner.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianhua, Qiu was appointed defense commissioner.

units.zh: 求暴病死，其將李彥圖自立，全播益懼，遂稱疾篤，杜門自絕。
units.en: Qiu died in a sudden fit of violence. His officer Li Yantu made himself chief. Quanbo, more afraid than ever, declared himself dying, barred his gate, and vanished from sight.
units.literal: Qiu died suddenly of violence. His general Li Yantu installed himself. Quanbo grew still more afraid, then claimed grave illness, shut his doors, and cut himself off.

units.zh: 彥圖疑之，使人覘其動靜，全播應覘為狀以自免。
units.en: Yantu did not trust the act and sent watchers. Quanbo played sick for them until they believed him.
units.literal: Yantu suspected him and sent men to spy on his movements; Quanbo answered the spies with displays of illness to save himself.

units.zh: 彥圖死，州人相率詣全播第，扣門請之，全播乃起，遣使請命於梁，拜防禦使。
units.en: Yantu died. The townspeople mobbed Quanbo’s gate and begged him to rule. Quanbo came out, sent word to Liang, and was made defense commissioner.
units.literal: When Yantu died, the people of the prefecture together went to Quanbo’s residence, knocked at the door and begged him; Quanbo then rose, sent envoys to submit to Liang, and was appointed defense commissioner.

units.zh: 全播治虔州七年，有善政，楊隆演遣劉信攻破虔州，以全播歸廣陵，卒年八十五。
units.en: Quanbo ruled Ganzhou seven years and governed well. Yang Longyan of Wu sent Liu Xin to take the city, carried Quanbo off to Guangling, and there he died at eighty-five.
units.literal: Quanbo governed Ganzhou seven years with good administration. Yang Longyan sent Liu Xin to break Ganzhou, took Quanbo back to Guangling, and he died at eighty-five.

units.zh: 當盧氏時，劉龑已取韶州，及全播被執，虔州遂入於吳。
units.en: Under the Lu clan Liu Yan had already seized Shaozhou. Once Quanbo was taken, Ganzhou passed to Wu.
units.literal: In Lu’s time Liu Yan had already taken Shaozhou; when Quanbo was captured, Ganzhou thereafter fell to Wu.

units.zh: 雷滿，武陵人也。
units.en: Lei Man came from Wuling.
units.literal: Lei Man was a native of Wuling.

units.zh: 為人兇悍獢勇，文身斷髪。
units.en: He was brutal, reckless, and wild—tattooed and shorn in the barbarian way.
units.literal: As a man he was fierce, reckless, and savage; his body was tattooed and his hair cut short.

units.zh: 唐廣明中，湖南饑，盜賊起，滿與同里人區景思、周嶽等聚諸蠻數千，獵於大澤中，乃擊鮮釃酒，擇坐中豪者，補置伍長，號土團軍，諸蠻從之，推滿為帥。
units.en: In the Guangming era famine gripped Hunan and outlaws multiplied. Man, Qu Jingsi, Zhou Yue, and others rallied thousands of hill folk, hunted the great marshes, feasted on fresh kill and strong wine, named the fiercest men squad leaders, and called the band the Native Corps. The tribes followed, and Man became their chief.
units.literal: In the Guangming era of Tang, Hunan suffered famine and bandits rose. Man with his fellow townsman Qu Jingsi, Zhou Yue, and others gathered several thousand barbarians, hunted in the great marshes, then slaughtered fresh meat and brewed wine, chose the boldest among those seated, appointed them squad chiefs, and styled the force the Native Corps; the barbarians followed, and Man was pushed as commander.

units.zh: 是時，高駢鎮荊南，召滿隸麾下，使以蠻軍擊賊。
units.en: Gao Pian then held Jingnan. He took Man into his service and set his barbarians on the bandits.
units.literal: At that time Gao Pian held Jingnan and summoned Man under his banner, ordering him to use barbarian troops against bandits.

units.zh: 駢徙淮南，滿從至廣陵，逃歸，殺刺史崔翥，遂據朗州，請命於唐。
units.en: When Pian moved to Huainan, Man followed him to Guangling, then bolted home, murdered the prefect Cui Zhu, seized Langzhou, and bowed to Tang.
units.literal: When Pian was transferred to Huainan, Man followed him to Guangling, then fled home, killed Prefect Cui Zhu, seized Langzhou, and submitted to Tang.

units.zh: 昭宗以澧、朗為武貞軍，拜滿節度使。
units.en: Zhaozong formed the Wuzhen circuit from Li and Lang and made Man its military commissioner.
units.literal: Zhaozong made Li and Lang the Wuzhen circuit and appointed Man military commissioner.

units.zh: 是時，澧陽人向瑰殺刺史呂自牧據澧州，而溪洞諸蠻宋鄴昌、師益等，皆起兵剽掠湖外，滿亦以輕舟上下荊江，攻劫州縣。
units.en: Xiang Gui of Liyang killed his prefect Lü Zimu and held Lizhou. Cave chiefs such as Song Yechang and Shi Yi raided the country beyond the lakes. Man skimmed the Yangzi in swift boats, sacking towns along the river.
units.literal: At that time Xiang Gui of Liyang killed Prefect Lü Zimu and held Lizhou, while the cave barbarians Song Yechang, Shi Yi, and others all raised troops to plunder beyond the lakes. Man too ranged the Jing River in light boats, attacking and robbing prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 楊行密攻杜洪於鄂州，荊南成汭出兵救洪，汭戰敗，溺死於君山。
units.en: Yang Xingmi besieged Du Hong at Ezhou. Cheng Ru of Jingnan sailed to his aid, was beaten, and drowned off Jun Hill.
units.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Du Hong at Ezhou. Cheng Ru of Jingnan marched to rescue Hong; Ru was defeated and drowned at Jun Hill.

units.zh: 滿襲破荊南，不能守，焚掠殆盡而去。
units.en: Man stormed Jingnan, could not keep it, burned what he could not carry, and left.
units.literal: Man raided and broke Jingnan but could not hold it; he burned and plundered nearly everything and departed.

units.zh: 滿嘗鑿深池於府中，客有過者，召宴池上，指其水曰：「蛟龍水怪皆窟於此，蓋水府也。」
units.en: Man dug a deep pool inside his yamen. When guests came he feasted them beside it and said, pointing at the water: “Dragons and river demons live down there. Call it a water palace.”
units.literal: Man once dug a deep pool in his headquarters. When a guest passed by, he would summon him to feast by the pool and, pointing at the water, say: “Dragons and water monsters all dwell here—it is a water palace.”

units.zh: 酒酣，取坐上器擲池中，因裸而入，取器嬉水上，久之乃出，治衣復坐，意氣自若。
units.en: Deep in wine he hurled tableware into the pool, stripped, dove after the pieces, played with them on the surface a long while, then climbed out, dressed, and sat down as calmly as before.
units.literal: When the wine ran deep he took vessels from the table and threw them into the pool, then stripped and went in, retrieved the vessels and sported on the water, and only after a long while came out, dressed himself, and sat again as if nothing had happened.

units.zh: 滿居朗州，引沅水塹其城，上為長橋，為不可攻之計。
units.en: Man made Langzhou his capital. He diverted the Yuan River to moat the walls and built a long bridge across it, planning to make the city impregnable.
units.literal: Man made his seat in Langzhou, diverted the Yuan River as a moat for his city, and built a long bridge above it as a plan to make it unassailable.

units.zh: 天祐中，滿卒，子彥恭自立。
units.en: During Tianyou Man died. His son Yan Gong seized power for himself.
units.literal: In the Tianyou era Man died, and his son Yan Gong installed himself.

units.zh: 彥恭附于楊行密，亦嘗攻劫為荊、湖患。
units.en: Yan Gong allied with Yang Xingmi but kept raiding as well, plaguing Jing and the lake country.
units.literal: Yan Gong submitted to Yang Xingmi but also raided and plundered, becoming a scourge to Jing and the lakes.

units.zh: 開平元年，馬殷發兵攻彥恭，恃塹為阻，逾年不能破。
units.en: In Kaiping 1 (907) Ma Yin marched on Yan Gong. The moat held them off for more than a year.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaiping Ma Yin sent troops to attack Yan Gong; relying on the moat as a barrier, for more than a year they could not break it.

units.zh: 三年，彥恭奔于楊行密，馬殷擒其弟彥雄等七人送于梁，斬于汴市，彥恭卒於淮南，澧、朗遂入于楚。
units.en: In year 3 Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin seized his brother Yan Xiong and six others, sent the seven captives to Liang, and had them beheaded in Bian. Yan Gong died in Huainan. Li and Lang passed to Chu.
units.literal: In the third year Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yan Xiong and others—seven men in all—sent them to Liang, and had them executed in the Bian market. Yan Gong died in Huainan, and Li and Lang thereafter fell to Chu.

units.zh: 鍾傳，洪州高安人也。
units.en: Zhong Chuan came from Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhong Chuan was a native of Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.

units.zh: 事州為小校，黃巢攻掠江淮，所在盜起，往往據州縣。
units.en: He was a petty officer of the prefecture. Huang Chao ravaged the Jiang-Huai; in his wake rebels seized town after town.
units.literal: He served the prefecture as a junior officer. Huang Chao swept the Jiang-Huai region; wherever he passed, bandits rose and often seized prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 傳以州兵擊賊，頻勝，遂逐觀察使，自稱留後。
units.en: Chuan beat the bandits again and again with prefectural troops, drove out the observation commissioner, and called himself acting governor.
units.literal: Chuan with prefectural troops attacked bandits and won repeatedly; he thereupon drove out the observation commissioner and styled himself acting military governor.

units.zh: 唐以洪州為鎮南軍，拜傳節度使。
units.en: Tang made Hong the Pacify-the-South circuit and named Chuan its commissioner.
units.literal: Tang made Hong Prefecture the Pacify-the-South circuit and appointed Chuan military commissioner.

units.zh: 江夏伶人杜洪者，亦據鄂州，楊行密屢攻之，洪頗倚傳為首尾。
units.en: Du Hong, a Jiangxia player turned warlord, held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi struck him again and again, and Hong counted on Chuan to guard his back.
units.literal: Du Hong, a Jiangxia actor, also held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi attacked him many times; Hong leaned heavily on Chuan as his rear support.

units.zh: 久之，洪敗死。
units.en: In time Hong was broken and killed.
units.literal: After a long while Hong was defeated and died.

units.zh: 是時，危全諷、韓師德等分據撫、吉諸州，傳皆不能節度，以兵攻之，稍聽命，獨全諷不能下，乃自率兵圍之。
units.en: Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others held Fu and Ji. Chuan could not rule them from afar; he marched on them until most bent the knee. Only Quanfeng held out, so Chuan went in person to besiege him.
units.literal: At that time Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others each held Fu and Ji prefectures. Chuan could not command them; he attacked with troops and they gradually submitted—only Quanfeng could not be brought down, and he therefore led troops himself to besiege him.

units.zh: 城中夜火起，諸將請急攻之，傳曰：「吾聞君子不迫人之危。」
units.en: Night fires flared inside the walls. His generals begged to storm the city. Chuan said: “A gentleman does not kick a man when he is down.”
units.literal: Fire broke out in the city by night. The generals asked for an urgent assault. Chuan said: “I have heard that a gentleman does not press a man in peril.”

units.zh: 乃掃地祭天，向城再拜，祝曰：「全諷不降，非民之罪，願天止火。」
units.en: He swept clean ground, offered to Heaven, bowed twice toward the walls, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not yield, the fault is not the people’s. Let the fire die.”
units.literal: He swept the ground and sacrificed to Heaven, bowed twice toward the city, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not submit, it is not the people’s crime—may Heaven halt the fire.”

units.zh: 全諷聞之，明日乃亦聽命，請以女妻傳子匡時。
units.en: Quanfeng heard the prayer. The next day he submitted and offered his daughter to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.
units.literal: When Quanfeng heard this, the next day he too submitted and asked to give his daughter in marriage to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.

units.zh: 傳居江西三十餘年，累拜太保、中書令，封南平王。
units.en: Chuan held Jiangxi for more than thirty years, rose to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and was made Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: Chuan dwelt in Jiangxi more than thirty years, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and enfeoffed Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 天祐三年，傳卒，子匡時自稱留後，請命於唐。
units.en: In Tianyou 3 (906) Chuan died. His son Kuangshi called himself acting governor and bowed to Tang.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Chuan died; his son Kuangshi styled himself acting military governor and submitted to Tang.

units.zh: 全諷曰：「聽鍾郎為節度使三年，吾將自為之。」
units.en: Quanfeng said: “I let Master Zhong be military commissioner three years; now I shall take the post myself.”
units.literal: Quanfeng said: “I let Master Zhong be military commissioner three years; now I shall take the post myself.”

units.zh: 已而傳養子延規與匡時爭立，乞兵於楊渥，渥遣秦裴等攻匡時，匡時敗，被執歸廣陵。
units.en: Soon Chuan’s adopted son Yangui fought Kuangshi for power and called on Yang Wo. Wo sent Qin Pei and others against Kuangshi, broke him, and carried him off to Guangling.
units.literal: Before long Chuan’s adopted son Yangui contended with Kuangshi for rule and begged troops from Yang Wo; Wo sent Qin Pei and others to attack Kuangshi. Kuangshi was defeated, seized, and taken to Guangling.

units.zh: 開平三年，全諷等起兵江西，謀復鍾氏故地，全諷為楊隆演將周本所敗，江西遂入於吳。
units.en: In Kaiping 3 (909) Quanfeng and his allies rose in Jiangxi to restore the Zhong domain. Yang Longyan’s general Zhou Ben crushed them, and Jiangxi passed to Wu.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, Quanfeng and others raised troops in Jiangxi to recover the Zhong clan’s old lands. Quanfeng was defeated by Yang Longyan’s general Zhou Ben, and Jiangxi thereafter fell to Wu.

units.zh: 趙匡凝
units.en: Zhao Kuangning
units.literal: Zhao Kuangning

units.zh: 趙匡凝，字光儀，蔡州人也。
units.en: Zhao Kuangning, styled Guangyi, came from Cai Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhao Kuangning, styled Guangyi, was a native of Cai Prefecture.

units.zh: 其父德諲事秦宗權，為申州刺史。
units.en: His father Zhao Dexin served Qin Zongquan and became prefect of Shen.
units.literal: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan and was made prefect of Shen.

units.zh: 宗權反，德諲攻下襄陽。
units.en: When Zongquan turned rebel, Dexin took Xiangyang.
units.literal: When Zongquan rebelled, Dexin captured Xiangyang.

units.zh: 梁太祖攻蔡州，宗權屢敗，德諲乃以山南東道七州降。
units.en: Zhu Wen attacked Cai again and again until Zongquan broke. Dexin then surrendered all seven prefectures of Shannan East.
units.literal: When Liang Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, Zongquan was repeatedly defeated; Dexin thereupon surrendered the seven prefectures of Shannan East Circuit.

units.zh: 梁太祖初鎮宣武，嘗為宗權所困，聞德諲降，大喜，表為行營副都統，河陽、保義、義昌三節度行軍司馬。
units.en: Zhu Wen, newly made lord of Xuanyi, had once been cornered by Zongquan. Dexin’s surrender delighted him. He made Dexin deputy supreme commander of the field army and liaison commissioner for Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.
units.literal: When Taizu first held Xuanyi, he had once been trapped by Zongquan; hearing of Dexin’s surrender, he rejoiced greatly and memorialized him as deputy supreme commander of the field army and military affairs commissioner for the three circuits of Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.

units.zh: 會其兵以攻蔡州，破之，德諲功多。
units.en: Dexin marched with him on Cai and helped break the city. His merit stood high.
units.literal: He then joined his troops to attack Cai Prefecture and broke it; Dexin’s merit was great.

units.zh: 德諲卒，子匡凝自立。
units.en: Dexin died, and Kuangning seized power for himself.
units.literal: When Dexin died, his son Kuangning installed himself.

units.zh: 是時，成汭死，雷彥恭襲取荊南，匡凝遣其弟匡明逐彥恭，太祖表匡凝荊襄節度使，以匡明為荊南留後。
units.en: Cheng Ru was dead and Lei Yan’gong had taken Jingnan. Kuangning sent his brother Kuangming to expel him. Zhu Wen made Kuangning commissioner of Jing-Xiang and Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.
units.literal: At that time Cheng Ru had died and Lei Yan’gong had seized Jingnan. Kuangning sent his younger brother Kuangming to drive out Yan’gong. Taizu memorialized Kuangning as military commissioner of Jing-Xiang and made Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.

units.zh: 是時，唐衰，藩鎮不復奉朝廷，獨匡凝兄弟貢賦不絕。
units.en: Tang was failing and the warlords had stopped paying the court—only the Kuangning brothers still sent tribute without fail.
units.literal: At that time Tang was in decline and the circuits no longer served the court; only the Kuangning brothers’ tribute and tax deliveries never ceased.

units.zh: 匡凝為人氣貌甚偉，性方嚴，喜自修飾，頗好學問，聚書數千卷，為政有威惠。
units.en: Kuangning was tall and stern, fastidious about his dress, fond of books, and kept libraries in the thousands. He ruled with iron and with mercy.
units.literal: Kuangning’s bearing was very imposing; his nature was upright and severe. He loved self-adornment, was quite fond of learning, gathered several thousand volumes of books, and in government combined sternness with kindness.

units.zh: 太祖攻兗州，朱瑾求救於晉，晉遣史儼等將兵數千救瑾，瑾敗，與儼等奔於淮南。
units.en: When Zhu Wen attacked Yan Prefecture, Zhu Jin begged Jin for aid; Jin sent Shi Yan and others with several thousand troops to rescue Zhu Jin. Zhu Jin was defeated and fled with Yan and the rest to Huainan.
units.literal: When Taizu attacked Yan Prefecture, Zhu Jin begged Jin for aid; Jin sent Shi Yan and others with several thousand troops to rescue Jin. Jin was defeated and fled with Yan and the rest to Huainan.

units.zh: 晉王李克用遣人以書幣假道於匡凝，以聘於楊行密，求歸儼等。
units.en: Li Keyong of Jin sent envoys with letters and gifts to ask passage through Kuangning’s lands and an audience with Yang Xingmi, seeking Yan and his men back.
units.literal: Prince of Jin Li Keyong sent men with letters and gifts to borrow a road through Kuangning and pay court to Yang Xingmi, seeking the return of Yan and the others.

units.zh: 晉王使者為梁得，太祖大怒。
units.en: Liang intercepted Jin’s envoys. Zhu Wen flew into a rage.
units.literal: Jin’s envoys were seized by Liang; Taizu was greatly enraged.

units.zh: 是時，梁已破兗、鄆，遣氏叔琮、康懷英等攻匡凝，叔琮取泌、隨二州，懷英取鄧州，匡凝懼，請盟，乃止。
units.en: Liang had already taken Yan and Yun. Zhu Wen sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying against Kuangning. Shuzong seized Bi and Sui; Huaiying took Deng. Kuangning sued for peace, and the assault stopped.
units.literal: At that time Liang had already broken Yan and Yun; it sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying and others to attack Kuangning. Shuzong took Bi and Sui prefectures; Huaiying took Deng. Kuangning was afraid and asked for peace, and the attack then ceased.

units.zh: 太祖弒昭宗，將謀代唐，畏匡凝兄弟不從，遣使告之，匡凝對使者流涕答曰：「受唐恩深，不敢妄有佗誌。」
units.en: When Zhu Wen killed Zhaozong and moved to take the throne, he feared the Kuangning brothers would refuse him. He sent word ahead. Kuangning wept before the envoys and said: “Tang’s kindness to me runs deep. I dare not dream of any other allegiance.”
units.literal: When Taizu murdered Zhaozong and was about to plot replacing Tang, he feared the Kuangning brothers would not follow and sent envoys to inform them. Kuangning wept before the envoys and answered: “I have received Tang’s grace deeply and dare not harbor any other design.”

units.zh: 太祖遣楊師厚攻之，太祖以兵殿漢北，匡凝戰敗，以輕舟奔於楊行密。
units.en: Zhu Wen sent Yang Shihou against him and marched in person on the Han north. Kuangning broke, took a light boat, and fled to Yang Xingmi.
units.literal: Taizu sent Yang Shihou to attack him; Taizu himself brought up the rear north of the Han River. Kuangning was defeated and fled in a light boat to Yang Xingmi.

units.zh: 師厚進攻荊南，匡明奔於蜀。
units.en: Shihou drove on Jingnan. Kuangming fled into Shu.
units.literal: Shihou pressed the attack on Jingnan; Kuangming fled to Shu.

units.zh: 匡凝至廣陵，行密見之，戲曰：「君在鎮時，輕車重馬，歲輸於梁，今敗乃歸我乎？」
units.en: At Guangling Yang Xingmi greeted him with a jest: “In your own domain you sent light carts and heavy horses every year to Liang. Broken now, you run to me?”
units.literal: When Kuangning reached Guangling, Xingmi saw him and jested: “When you held your circuit you sent light carts and heavy horses each year to Liang—now defeated, you come to me?”

units.zh: 匡凝曰：「僕世為唐臣，歲時職貢，非輸賊也。
units.en: Kuangning said: “My house has been Tang’s for generations. The yearly gifts were tribute owed the throne, not tribute to a thief.
units.literal: Kuangning said: “Your servant’s house has served Tang for generations; the yearly tribute was duty, not payment to a bandit.

units.zh: 今以不從賊之故，力屈歸公，惟公生死之耳！」
units.en: I would not follow the usurper, and here I am, spent. Do with me as you will!”
units.literal: Now for refusing the bandit I am spent and come to you—only live or die is yours to decide!”

units.zh: 行密厚遇之。
units.en: Yang Xingmi treated him with honor.
units.literal: Xingmi treated him generously.

units.zh: 其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。
units.en: When Xingmi died, his son Yang Wo grew cold toward him.
units.literal: Afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo grew somewhat discourteous toward him.

units.zh: 渥方宴，食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。」
units.en: Wo was feasting on green plums when Kuangning looked over and said: “Don’t eat too many. They heat a child’s blood.”
units.literal: Wo was at feast eating green plums when Kuangning glanced at Wo and said: “Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children.”

units.zh: 諸將以為慢，渥遷匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。
units.en: The officers read it as insult. Wo banished him to Hailing. Later Xu Wen had him killed.
units.literal: The generals thought it insolent. Wo moved Kuangning to Hailing; later Xu Wen had him killed.

units.zh: 匡明卒於蜀。
units.en: Kuangming died in Shu.
units.literal: Kuangming died in Shu.

units.zh: 復領兵萬餘人渡淮討楊行密，至濠州，聞龐師古清口之敗，遽班師。
units.en: Crossing the Huai against Yang Xingmi he withdrew on news of Qingkou.
units.literal: Again he led more than ten thousand troops across the Huai to attack Yang Xingmi; reaching Haozhou he heard of Pang Shigu's defeat at Qingkou and hastily withdrew the army.

units.zh: 黃巢滅，淮、蔡間秦宗權復盛，朝廷以淮、蔡與汴州相接，太祖汴人，必究其能否，遂移授宣武軍節度使以討宗權，未凡滅之。
units.en: After Huang Chao fell, Qin Zongquan rose again between Huai and Cai; because those regions marched with Bian and Taizu was a native of Bian, the court had to try him and transferred him as Xuanwu commissioner to destroy Zongquan—which he soon did.
units.literal: When Huang Chao was destroyed, Qin Zongquan revived his strength between Huai and Cai; the court, because Huai and Cai bordered Bianzhou and Taizu was a man of Bian, was bound to test his ability, and so transferred him as Xuanwu Military Commissioner to attack Zongquan; before long he destroyed him.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 山南東道節度使楊師厚進納越匡凝東第書籍。
units.en: Yang Shihou of Shannan East surrendered the library of Yue Kuangning's eastern mansion.
units.literal: Yang Shihou, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, presented and surrendered the books of Yue Kuangning's eastern mansion.

units.zh: 先是，收復襄、漢，帝閱其圖書，至是命師厚進焉。
units.en: When Xiangyang and Hanzhong were retaken the Emperor had browsed these books; now he ordered Shihou to deliver them.
units.literal: Earlier, when Xiang and Han were recovered, the Emperor had examined these books; now he ordered Shihou to present them.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 帝遣陝州康懷英、華州寇彥卿率兵攻迫邠、寧，以緩朔方之寇。
units.en: The Emperor sent Kang Huaiying of Shaan and Kou Yanqing of Hua to strike Bin and Ning and ease the Shuofang threat.
units.literal: The Emperor sent Shaan Prefecture’s Kang Huaiying and Hua Prefecture’s Kou Yanqing to attack Bin and Ning to relieve pressure on Shuofang.

units.zh: 陝州康懷英侵秦，克甯、慶、衍三州。
units.en: Kang Huaiying of Shaan attacked Qin and took Ning, Qing, and Yan.
units.literal: Kang Huaiying of Shaan invaded Qin and captured Ning, Qing, and Yan prefectures.

units.zh: 秦人來襲，懷英兵敗於升平。
units.en: Qin struck back and Huaiying was beaten at Shengping.
units.literal: Qin forces counterattacked and Huaiying was defeated at Shengping.

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 初收兗、鄆，得朱瑾妻，溫告之曰：「彼既無依，寓於輜車。」
units.en: After the capture of Yan and Yun they took Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her travel in the supply train."
units.literal: When Yan and Yun were first taken, they obtained Zhu Jin’s wife; Wen told her: "She has no one to rely on—let her lodge in the baggage train."

units.zh: 張氏遣人召之，瑾妻再拜，張氏答拜泣下，謂之曰：「兗、鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故尋戈，致吾姒如此。
units.en: Zhang sent for her; Jin’s wife bowed low, Zhang bowed back in tears and said: "Yan and Yun share our house’s surname—brothers quarreled over a trifle, and you, my sister-in-law, suffer for it.
units.literal: Zhang sent someone to summon her; Jin’s wife bowed twice, Zhang returned the bow weeping, and said to her: "Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Minister of Works; between brothers a small quarrel drew swords, and my sister-in-law has come to this.

units.zh: 又泣下，乃度為尼，張恒給其費。
units.en: Weeping again, she had Jin’s wife take the veil and paid her upkeep.
units.literal: Again she wept, then had her tonsured as a nun; Zhang constantly supplied her expenses.

units.zh: 辛未，武安軍節度使馬殷進封楚王。
units.en: On xinwei Ma Yin, governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced to King of Chu.
units.literal: On xinwei, Ma Yin, military governor of the Wu'an Army, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Chu.

units.zh: 及死，子彥恭繼之。
units.en: At his death his son Yiangong took over.
units.literal: When he died, his son Yiangong succeeded him.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：滿以天復元年卒，子彥威自立，弟彥恭結忠義節度使趙匡凝以逐彥威。）〉
units.en: (The New Tang History says: Man died in Tianfu 1; his son Yanwei established himself; Yanwei's younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man died in Tianfu year 1; son Yanwei established himself; younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)〉

units.zh: 殷極其兵力，攻圍周歲，彥恭食盡兵敗，間使求救於淮夷。
units.en: Yin besieged a full year; starving and beaten, Yiangong sent to the Huai for aid.
units.literal: Yin exhausted his military strength; attack and siege a full year; Yiangong food exhausted, troops defeated, through envoys begged rescue from the Huai barbarians.

units.zh: 及淮軍來援，高季昌逆戰於治津馬頭岸，大破之，俄而攻陷朗州，彥恭單棹遁去。
units.en: When Huai reinforcements came, Gao Jichang routed them at Matou Bank, then took Langzhou as Yiangong fled alone in a skiff.
units.literal: When Huai troops came to rescue, Gao Jichang met them in battle at Zhijin Matou Bank and greatly defeated them; soon he attacked and took Lang prefecture; Yiangong in a single punt fled away.

units.zh: 蠻蜒狡獪，深有父風，燼墟落，榜舟楫，上下於南郡、武昌之間，殆無人矣。
units.en: Savage and sly like his father, he burned villages and raided by boat between Nanjun and Wuchang until hardly anyone remained.
units.literal: A crafty southern barbarian, deeply having his father's manner: burning ruins and villages, plying boats and oars, up and down between Nanjun and Wuchang—nearly no people remained.

units.zh: 又與淮、蜀結連，阻絕王命。
units.en: He allied with Huai and Shu and blocked the court's orders.
units.literal: Again he linked with Huai and Shu, obstructing and cutting off the royal commands.

units.zh: 馬殷擒其弟彥雄及逆黨七人，械送至闕，皆斬於汴橋下，時開平二年十一月也。
units.en: Ma Yin seized Yanxiong and seven rebels, sent them to Bian—all were executed at Bian Bridge in Kaiping 2, month 11.
units.literal: Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yanxiong and seven rebel partisans, sent them in shackles to the capital—all were beheaded below Bian Bridge; it was Kaiping year 2, eleventh month.

units.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。
units.en: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as right regular attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.

units.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。
units.en: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.
units.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
units.en: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Academy, commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and commissioner for salt and iron transport across all circuits.
units.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Academy, Commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport across all circuits.

units.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。
units.en: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made acting right vice director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.

units.zh: 初，澧、朗二州，本屬荊南，乾寧中，為土豪雷滿所據。
units.en: Li and Lang, once part of Jingnan, fell to the local strongman Lei Man in Qianning.
units.literal: At first Li and Lang two prefectures originally belonged to Jingnan; in Qianning they were held by local strongman Lei Man.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：滿字秉仁。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Tang History》 gives his style as Bingren.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man's style name was Bingren.)〉

units.zh: 中和初，擅率部兵自廣陵逃歸於朗，沿江恣殘暴，始為荊人大患矣。
units.en: Early Zhonghe he deserted Guangling for Langzhou and raided the Yangzi—Jing's nightmare had begun.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe he on his own led his troops to flee from Guangling back to Lang, along the river wantonly cruel and violent, beginning to be a great affliction to the people of Jing.

units.zh: 始為朗州小校，唐廣明初，王仙芝焚劫江陵。
units.en: He began as a Langzhou corporal; when Wang Xianzhi sacked Jiangling in early Guangming,
units.literal: At first he was a petty officer of Lang prefecture; at the beginning of Tang Guangming, Wang Xianzhi burned and plundered Jiangling.

units.zh: 武陵洞蠻也。
units.en: came from the Wuling cave tribes.
units.literal: was a cave-barbarian of Wuling.

units.zh: 唐朝姑務息兵，即以澧朗節度使授之。
units.en: Tang bought peace and gave him the Li-Lang commission.
units.literal: The Tang court for the moment pursued resting arms and thereupon granted him the Li and Lang military commissioner.

units.zh: 滿貪穢慘毒，蓋非人類。
units.en: Man's greed and cruelty were scarcely human.
units.literal: Man was greedy, foul, and cruelly poisonous—surely no human kind.

units.zh: 又嘗於府署浚一深潭，構大亭於其上，每鄰道使車經由，必召宴於中，且言：「此水府也，中有蛟龍，奇怪萬態，惟餘能遊焉。」
units.en: He dug a deep pool at headquarters and built a pavilion over it; when envoys passed through he always feasted them there and boasted, "This is my water palace, full of dragons in ten thousand shapes—only I can swim it."
units.literal: Again he once at the prefectural office dug a deep pool, built a great pavilion upon it; whenever neighboring circuit envoys' carriages passed through, he inevitably summoned them to feast within, and moreover said: "This is the water palace; within are flood-dragons, myriad strange forms—only I can roam it."

units.zh: 雷滿者，偏州一草賊爾，令公盍不加兵，而反怨朝廷乎！」
units.en: Yet you resent the court over Lei Man, a mere frontier bandit—why not march against him instead?"
units.literal: Lei Man is but a petty prefecture grass bandit—why does my lord not send troops instead of resenting the court!"

units.zh: 雷滿，
units.en: Lei Man,
units.literal: Lei Man,

units.zh: 是時，朝廷以高駢為節度使，駢擢滿為裨將，以領蠻軍。
units.en: the court sent Gao Pian as commissioner, and Pian made Man a deputy to lead tribal levies.
units.literal: At that time the court appointed Gao Pian military commissioner; Pian promoted Man to deputy general to lead barbarian troops.

units.zh: 駢移鎮淮南，復隸部曲，以悍獷趫健知名。
units.en: When Pian moved south, Man stayed in his retinue and won fame for ferocious speed.
units.literal: When Pian shifted his garrison to Huainan, Man again belonged to his command; for fierce and unruly speed and strength he was famed.

units.zh: 九月丙寅，製削奪廣州節度使、南平王劉岩在身官爵，以其將謀僭號故也。
units.en: On bingyin in the ninth month the court stripped Liu Yan of Guang and his Prince of Nanping title for impending usurpation.
units.literal: On bingyin in the ninth month an order stripped Guang military commissioner and Prince of Nanping Liu Yan of all offices and ranks he held, because he was about to usurp a title.

units.zh: 仍詔天下兵馬元帥錢鏐指揮攻討。
units.en: Qian Liu, marshal of all armies, was ordered to lead the punitive campaign.
units.literal: An edict still ordered marshal of all armies Qian Liu to direct the attack.

units.zh: 是月，劉鄩攻下兗州，擒張守進，夷其族。
units.en: That month Liu Xun took Yan, captured Zhang Shoujin, and exterminated his clan.
units.literal: That month Liu Xun captured Yan Prefecture, seized Zhang Shoujin, and exterminated his clan.

units.zh: 及成汭敗於鄂州，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui fell at Ezhou, Kuangning had his brother Kuangming made acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated at E prefecture, Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 匡凝弟匡明，字讚堯，幼以父貴，一子出身，為江陵府文學。
units.en: His brother Kuangming, styled Zanyao, entered office young as a literary officer at Jiangling through their father's rank.
units.literal: Kuangning's younger brother Kuangming, style name Zanyao, in youth by his father's eminence entered office as a single son—he was Jiangling prefecture literary officer.

units.zh: 及建稱帝，用為大理卿、工部尚書。
units.en: When Wang Jian became emperor he made him Grand Court director and Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Jian declared himself emperor, he used him as Grand Court of Review director and Works Ministry minister.

units.zh: 及壯，以軍功曆繡、峽二州刺史。
units.en: Grown, he won military merit as inspector of Xiuxi and Xia.
units.literal: When grown, by military merit he passed through Xiuxi and Xia prefecture inspector posts.

units.zh: 天祐二年秋七月，遣楊師厚率師討之。
units.en: In autumn, month 7 of Tianyou 2, he sent Yang Shihou to attack him.
units.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn seventh month, he sent Yang Shihou to lead troops to attack him.

units.zh: 匡明亦謀奔淮南，子承規諫曰：「昔諸葛兄弟分仕二國，若適揚州，是自取疑也。」
units.en: Kuangming meant to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui warned, "Like the Zhuge brothers serving rival states, going to Yangzhou would invite suspicion."
units.literal: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui remonstrated: "In old times the Zhuge brothers each served a different state—if you go to Yangzhou, it is yourself inviting suspicion."

units.zh: 成汭之敗，其兄匡凝表為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui's defeat his brother made him acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated, his elder brother Kuangning memorialized him as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 久之，卒於蜀。
units.en: He died in Shu many years later.
units.literal: After long time he died in Shu.

units.zh: 匡明謂然，乃趨成都。
units.en: Kuangming agreed and fled to Chengdu instead.
units.literal: Kuangming thought it so and thereupon hastened to Chengdu.

units.zh: 匡明領兵逐之，遂鎮於渚宮。
units.en: Kuangming drove them off and held court at Zhugong.
units.literal: Kuangming led troops to drive them off and then held commission at Zhugong.

units.zh: 匡明懼，乃舉族上峽奔蜀，王建待以賓禮。
units.en: Kuangming fled upriver to Shu with his clan; Wang Jian received him as an honored guest.
units.literal: Kuangming feared and thereupon led his clan up the gorge to flee to Shu; Wang Jian received him with guest ceremony.

units.zh: 成汭，淮西人。
units.en: Cheng Rui came from west of the Huai.
units.literal: Cheng Rui was a native of Huai West.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：入蔡賊中，為賊帥假子，更姓名為郭禹。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says he joined the Cai rebels as an adopted son and renamed himself Guo Yu.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: entering Cai rebel bands, he became a rebel chief's adoptive son and changed his name to Guo Yu.)〉

units.zh: 少年任俠，乘醉殺人，為仇家所捕，因落發為僧，冒姓郭氏。
units.en: As a young man he killed someone in a drunken brawl, was hunted by the victim's kin, shaved his head as a monk, and took the surname Guo.
units.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold, killed a man while drunk, was seized by the enemy family, and therefore shaved his head to become a monk and usurped the surname Guo.

units.zh: 汭嘗仇殺人，懼為吏所捕，改姓郭氏。
units.en: After a feud killing he had taken the surname Guo to evade the law.
units.literal: Rui once killed in feud; fearing capture by officers, changed surname to Guo.

units.zh: 後據歸州，招集流亡，練士伍，得兵千餘人，沿流以襲荊南，遂據其地。
units.en: He took Guizhou, rallied refugees into a thousand-man force, sailed downriver against Jingnan, and seized it.
units.literal: Later he seized Guizhou, gathered fugitives, drilled soldiers, obtained more than a thousand troops, along the river struck Jingnan, and thus held that territory.

units.zh: 唐僖宗朝，為蔡州軍校，領本郡兵戍荊南，帥以其凶暴，欲害之，遂棄本軍奔於秭歸。
units.en: Under Xizong he was a Caizhou officer garrisoning Jingnan until his commander, fearing his violence, tried to kill him; he fled to Zigui with his troops.
units.literal: In Emperor Xizong's Tang he was a Cai prefecture army officer, led the prefecture's troops to garrison Jingnan; the commander because of his ferocity wished to harm him, so he abandoned his army and fled to Zigui.

units.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖以汭歿於王事，上表於唐帝，請為汭立廟於荊門，優詔可之。
units.en: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder had the Tang court approve a temple for Rui at Jingmen, honoring his death in service.
units.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder because Rui died in royal service memorialized the Tang emperor requesting a temple for Rui at Jingmen; gracious edict approved.

units.zh: 亡匿久之，及貴，方復本姓。
units.en: He lived in hiding for years and only restored his true name once he had risen.
units.literal: He hid in flight a long time; when he reached eminence he then restored his original surname.

units.zh: 及為荊南節度使，命準為表，乞歸本姓。
units.en: As Jingnan commissioner he had Zhun draft a memorial to restore the name Cheng.
units.literal: When he became Jingnan military commissioner, ordered Zhun to draft a memorial begging restoration of original surname.

units.zh: 又云：「成為本姓，郭乃冒稱。
units.en: It added, "Cheng is my true name; Guo was a borrowed lie.
units.literal: Also said: "Cheng is the original surname; Guo is usurped claim.

units.zh: 伏乞聖慈，許歸本姓」云云。
units.en: I kneel and beg Your Majesty to let me bear my true name again," and so on.
units.literal: Kneeling beg sacred kindness, permit restoration of original surname," etc.

units.zh: 累官至檢校太尉，封上穀郡王。
units.en: He rose to honorary Grand Commandant and was made Prince of Shanggu.
units.literal: In succession he reached honorary Grand General and was enfeoffed Prince of Shanggu commandery.

units.zh: 楊行密以兵圍鄂州，汭出師以援鄂，淮寇乘之，以火焚其艦，汭投江而死。
units.en: When Yang Xingmi besieged Ezhou, Rui sailed to relieve it; the Huainan fleet burned his ships and he drowned himself in the river.
units.literal: Yang Xingmi with troops besieged Ezhou; Rui marched out to relieve E; Huainan raiders seized the moment, used fire to burn his warships; Rui threw himself in the river and died.

units.zh: 未至夏口，汭敗溺死，淮人遂陷鄂州，洪為其所擒，被害於廣陵市，時唐天復二年也。
units.en: Rui drowned in defeat before Xiakou; the Huainan army took Ezhou, seized Hong, and executed him at Guangling market in Tianfu 2.
units.literal: Before reaching Xiakou, Rui was defeated and drowned; Huainan men then took Ezhou; Hong was captured by them, killed at Guangling market—then Tang Tianfu year 2.

units.zh: 汭性豪暴，事皆意斷，又好自矜伐，騁辯淩人，深為識者所鄙。
units.en: Rui was domineering, arrogant in debate, and widely scorned by men of judgment.
units.literal: Rui's nature was arrogant and violent; affairs were all decided by his own intent; he also loved self-praise, vaunted eloquence to overbear others, and was deeply despised by the knowing.

units.zh: 一夕，巨蛇繞其身，幾至於殞，乃祝曰：「苟有所負，死生惟命。」
units.en: One night a giant snake coiled around him until he nearly died; he prayed, "If I am guilty, let fate decide."
units.literal: One night a huge serpent coiled around his body, almost to his death; he then prayed, saying: "If I bear some guilt, life and death are fate's alone."

units.zh: 是時荊州經巨盜之後，居民才一十七家，汭撫輯凋殘，勵精為理，通商訓農，勤於惠養，比及末年，僅及萬戶。
units.en: Jingzhou after the great devastations held only seventeen households; Rui rebuilt trade and agriculture until, by his last years, the city neared ten thousand families.
units.literal: At that time Jingzhou after great bandits had only seventeen resident households; Rui pacified the devastated ruin, strove in governance, opened commerce and trained farming, diligently in nurturing kindness—by his last years barely reaching ten thousand households.

units.zh: 汭奏請割隸，唐宰相徐彥若執而不行，汭由是銜之。
units.en: Rui asked the court to annex them; Chancellor Xu Yanruo refused, and Rui nursed a grudge.
units.literal: Rui memorialized requesting to detach and subordinate them; Tang chancellor Xu Yanruo held firm and did not carry it out; Rui thereby harbored resentment.

units.zh: 及彥若出鎮南海，路過江陵，汭雖加延接，而猶怏怏。
units.en: When Yanruo passed Jiangling en route to his Nanhai post, Rui received him coldly despite the courtesies.
units.literal: When Yanruo went out to command Nanhai, passing Jiangling, Rui though adding courtesies was still displeased.

units.zh: 汭赧然而屈。
units.en: Rui flushed and fell silent.
units.literal: Rui blushed and was subdued.

units.zh: 成汭鎮荊南，辟為推官。
units.en: When Cheng Rui held Jingnan he made Zhun his investigating officer.
units.literal: Cheng Rui garrisoned Jingnan and recruited him as investigating officer.

units.zh: 後因汭生辰，淮南楊行密遣使致禮幣之外，仍貺《初學記》一部。
units.en: On Rui's birthday Yang Xingmi sent gifts from Huainan—and added a copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.
units.literal: Later because of Rui's birthday Huainan Yang Xingmi sent envoys with ceremonial gifts besides, still bestowing one copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.

units.zh: 準忿然以為不可，謂汭曰：「夫《初學記》，蓋訓童之書爾，今敵國交聘，以此書為貺，得非相輕之甚耶！
units.en: Zhun was furious and told Rui, "The 《Elementary Studies》 is a schoolbook for children. An enemy state sends it as a state gift—is that not open contempt?
units.literal: Zhun angrily deemed it unacceptable, told Rui: "The 《Elementary Studies》 is merely a book for instructing children; now enemy states exchange missions—using this book as a gift, is it not extreme mutual slight!

units.zh: 汭不納，準自歎曰：「若然，見輕敵國，足彰幕府之無人也。
units.en: Rui refused. Zhun sighed, "Accept this and we show the enemy our staff has no one with spine.
units.literal: Rui did not accept; Zhun sighed to himself: "If so, being slighted by the enemy state sufficiently shows the headquarters has no men.

units.zh: 汭怒其去，潛使人於途中殺之。）〉
units.en: Rui, enraged, had him murdered on the road home.)〉
units.literal: Rui angry at his departure, secretly sent men on the road to kill him.)〉

units.zh: 太祖命荊南成汭率荊、襄舟師以赴之。
units.en: The Founder ordered Cheng Rui of Jingnan to sail the Jing-Xiang fleet to his aid.
units.literal: The Founder ordered Jingnan Cheng Rui to lead Jing and Xiang river fleets to go relieve.

units.zh: 及賊巢渡江，罕之因以兵將背賊歸於唐，高駢錄其功，表為光州刺史。
units.en: When Chao crossed the Yangzi he defected to Tang; Gao Pian made him Guang commissioner.
units.literal: When bandit Chao crossed the river, Hanzhi therefore with troops turned his back on the bandits and returned to Tang; Gao Pian recorded his merit and memorialized him Guang prefecture military commissioner.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·秦裴傳》：天祐三年，洪州鍾傳卒，州人立其子匡時。
units.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that in Tianyou 3 Zhong Chuan died at Hongzhou and the people set up his son Kuangshi.)
units.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Qin Pei》: Tianyou year 3, Hongzhou Zhong Chuan died; the prefecture's people installed his son Kuangshi.

units.zh: 江州刺史延規，傳之養子，忿不得立，以其郡納款，因授裴西南面行營招討使，攻匡時。
units.en: Yan Gui, Chuan's adopted son and Jiangzhou prefect, resenting his exclusion, surrendered his prefecture; Qin Pei was sent to attack Kuangshi.
units.literal: Jiangzhou prefect Yan Gui, Chuan's adoptive son, angry at not being installed, submitted his prefecture in surrender; therefore Pei was appointed southwest campaign pacification commissioner and attacked Kuangshi.

units.zh: 友倫與氏叔琮等躡其轍，追至太原，摩壘挑戰，獲牛馬萬餘。
units.en: With Shi Shuzong he pursued to Taiyuan, challenged the walls, and seized more than ten thousand cattle and horses.
units.literal: You Lun with Shi Shuzong and others followed their tracks, pursuing to Taiyuan, pressing the ramparts and challenging battle, obtaining more than ten thousand cattle and horses.

units.zh: 天復元年，岐、隴用兵，晉人乘虛侵於北鄙。
units.en: In Tianfu 1, while war raged at Qi and Long, Jin raiders struck the northern border.
units.literal: In Tianfu year 1, troops were used at Qi and Long; Jin men took advantage of emptiness to invade the northern frontier.

units.zh: 趙匡凝，
units.en: Next was Zhao Kuangning,
units.literal: Zhao Kuangning,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：匡凝字光儀。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 gives his style as Guangyi.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Kuangning's style name was Guangyi.)〉

units.zh: 及德諲卒，匡凝自為襄州留後，朝廷即以旄鉞授之。
units.en: When Dexin died Kuangning made himself acting commissioner and received the court commission.
units.literal: When Dexin died, Kuangning made himself Xiangzhou acting commissioner; the court thereupon bestowed the command baton and axe.

units.zh: 匡凝以父功為唐州刺史兼七州馬步軍都校。
units.en: Kuangning became Tang prefect inspector and overall commander of seven prefectures' horse and foot through his father's merit.
units.literal: Kuangning by his father's merit was Tang prefecture inspector and concurrent seven-prefecture horse-and-foot army overall commander.

units.zh: 唐光啟四年夏六月，德諲審宗權必敗，乃舉漢南之地以歸唐朝，仍遣使投分於太祖，兼誓戮力，同討宗權。
units.en: In summer, month 6 of Guangqi 4, Dexin saw Zongquan would fall, surrendered Hannan to Tang, sent envoys to the Founder, and swore to destroy Zongquan together.
units.literal: Tang Guangqi year 4 summer sixth month, Dexin judged Zongquan would surely be defeated and thereupon raised the Hannan lands to return to Tang, still sending envoys to declare separation to the Founder and jointly swearing united strength to attack Zongquan together.

units.zh: 蔡州人也。
units.en: was a native of Cai prefecture.
units.literal: was a man of Cai prefecture.

units.zh: 匡凝氣貌甚偉，好自修飾，每整衣冠，必使人持巨鑒前後照之。
units.en: Tall and vain, he had great mirrors held before and behind him whenever he dressed.
units.literal: Kuangning's bearing was very grand; he loved self-adornment—each time he arranged cap and robes he must have men hold great mirrors before and behind to shine on him.

units.zh: 對客之際，烏巾上微覺有塵，即令侍妓持紅拂以去之。
units.en: If he sensed dust on his black cap before guests, maids brushed it away with red dusters.
units.literal: When facing guests, on the black cap he slightly sensed dust and at once ordered serving girls to hold red dusters to remove it.

units.zh: 八月，太祖親領大軍南征，仍請削匡凝在身官爵。
units.en: Month 8 the Founder marched south in person and had Kuangning stripped of rank.
units.literal: Eighth month, the Founder personally led a great army south on campaign and still requested stripping Kuangning of his personal offices and titles.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：行密厚遇匡凝，其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。
units.en: Ouyang's 《History》 says Xingmi treated Kuangning well, but after Xingmi's death Yang Wo grew rude to him.
units.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》 says: Xingmi treated Kuangning generously; afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo gradually was without courtesy to him.

units.zh: 諸將以為慢，渥遣匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。）〉
units.en: Officers took it as insult; Wo exiled him to Hailing, where Xu Wen later killed him.)〉
units.literal: The generals thought it disrespect; Wo sent Kuangning to Hailing and later Xu Wen killed him.)〉

units.zh: 初，匡凝好聚書，及敗，楊師厚獲數千卷於第，悉以來獻。
units.en: Kuangning had loved books; after his defeat Shihou seized thousands of scrolls from his house and presented them to the Founder.
units.literal: At first Kuangning loved gathering books; when defeated, Yang Shihou obtained several thousand scrolls at his residence and entirely brought them as tribute.

units.zh: 匡凝對使者流涕，答以受國恩深，豈敢隨時妄有他誌。
units.en: Kuangning wept before the envoy and said the state's grace was too deep for him to change sides with the times.
units.literal: Kuangning to the envoy wept and replied that the state's grace was deep—how dare he follow the times and rashly have another intent.

units.zh: 渥方宴食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。」
units.en: At a feast Wo ate green plums; Kuangning warned, "Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children."
units.literal: Wo was just feasting and eating green plums; Kuangning looked at Wo and said: "Do not eat much—it brings children's fever."

units.zh: 光化初，匡凝以太祖有清口之敗，密附於淮夷，太祖遣氏叔琮率師伐之。
units.en: Early in Guanghua, after the Founder's defeat at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly sided with the Huai rebels and the Founder sent Shi Shucong against him.
units.literal: At the start of Guanghua, because the Founder had been defeated at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly attached himself to the Huai forces; the Founder sent Shi Shucong with troops to attack him.

units.zh: 俄而康懷英攻下鄧州，匡凝懼，遣使乞盟，太祖許之，自是附庸於太祖。
units.en: Kang Huaiying took Deng; Kuangning sued for peace, the Founder agreed, and he became a vassal.
units.literal: Soon Kang Huaiying attacked and took Deng prefecture; Kuangning feared and sent envoys to beg alliance—the Founder permitted it; from then he was a vassal of the Founder.

units.zh: 是時唐室微弱，諸道常賦多不上供，惟匡凝昆仲雖強據江山，然盡忠帝室，貢賦不絕。
units.en: While Tang weakened and most circuits withheld tribute, the Zhao brothers still sent loyal levies from their strongholds.
units.literal: At that time the Tang house was weak; many circuits' regular levies often did not go up in tribute—only Kuangning and his brothers, though strongly holding rivers and mountains, yet were wholly loyal to the imperial house and tribute and levies did not cease.

units.zh: 太祖將期受禪，以匡凝兄弟並據藩鎮，乃遣使先諭旨焉。
units.en: As the Founder prepared to take the throne, he sent envoys ahead to the Zhao brothers holding the frontier commands.
units.literal: The Founder was about to fix the date to receive the abdication mandate; because Kuangning and his brothers both held frontier commissions, he sent envoys first to announce the intent.

units.zh: 及師厚濟江，匡凝以兵數萬逆戰，大為師厚所敗，匡凝乃燔其舟，單舸急棹，沿漢而遁於金陵。
units.en: Shihou crossed the river; Kuangning met him with tens of thousands, was routed, burned his fleet, and fled alone up the Han to Jinling.
units.literal: When Shihou crossed the river, Kuangning with tens of thousands of troops met him in battle and was greatly defeated by Shihou; Kuangning then burned his boats, in a single skiff urgently rowed, and along the Han fled to Jinling.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：師厚由陰穀伐木為梁，匡凝以兵二萬瀕江戰，大敗，乃燔州，單舸夜奔揚州。
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou bridged Yin Valley, Kuangning lost twenty thousand along the river, burned the prefecture, and fled by night to Yangzhou.
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou by Yin Valley felled timber for beams; Kuangning with twenty thousand troops fought along the river, was greatly defeated, then burned the prefecture and in a single skiff fled by night to Yangzhou.
